title: Margaret Mead's birth chart
metaDescription: Margaret Mead's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.1° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Jupiter sit 0.6° from an exact conjunction — near enough that the tradition reads drive and expansion as a single working part. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 24.1° Sagittarius. That falls in the third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Sagittarius (14.9°), Venus in Aquarius (10.8°), Mars in Capricorn (17.3°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Uranus opposition Pluto, 0.0° of separation. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mars conjunction Jupiter at 0.6°, and Mars conjunction Saturn at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 14.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Capricorn at 17.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Capricorn at 17.9° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Capricorn at 15.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: fire 3, earth 3, air 2, water 1 across the elements, and mutable 4, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modalities. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.0° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
